body:
A smaller alternative to duckdb/duckdb#28639. It fixes the same two v2.0 regressions after delim joins became materialized CTEs: a lateral UNNEST runs out of memory, and a `json_valid` guard stops protecting a lateral table function in a correlated subquery. It uses the same two planner changes as duckdb/duckdb#28639 and leaves out the third.

**Kept from duckdb/duckdb#28639**
- `CanRestrictCorrelationDomain` now accepts `LOGICAL_UNNEST` and table in-out functions that are not volatile and have no final step. The CTE filter pusher can then move a guard on the outer rows into their input. This alone fixes the Malformed JSON errors for `range`, `unnest` and `json_each`.
- The rewrite no longer wraps its two CTEs in identity projections (added in eb35d40269c for column pruning, which `RemoveUnusedColumns` now handles for materialized CTEs). A filter that can throw therefore no longer stops at a projection that isn't a query block boundary, and reaches the UNNEST output. This fixes the OOM. duckdb/duckdb#28639 used a projection flag for this instead.

**Left out**
- Running `EMPTY_RESULT_PULLUP` again after statistics propagation, together with the anti-join projection-map change it needs. On main this case already takes about 0.01 s (3M rows, the view example in duckdb/duckdb#28639). The extra pass also changed which errors get raised, and it forced edits to 4 unrelated tests (`deliminator.test`, `scalar_aggregate_merge_tpcds_plan.test`, `test_window_self_join.test`, `updating_the_join_node_hash_map_has_no_errors.test_slow`). None of those tests change here.
- The two new test files are merged into one, `test/sql/subquery/lateral/lateral_filter_into_delim_cte.test`, without `PRAGMA enable_verification`. The file is skipped under `verify_serializer` and `disable_optimizer`, as in duckdb/duckdb#28639, because both drop the planner-only marks.

**Extra test**
- The new test also runs an `EXPLAIN` check that a wide table scanned under a delim join CTE still projects only the columns it needs (`id, pad1`), plus a result check on the same query. This confirms that dropping the identity projections keeps column pruning.

**Results** (reldebug, before → after)

| query | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| lateral UNNEST + throwing filter, 4 GB limit | Out of Memory | 20 rows counted, 0.34 s |
| `NOT EXISTS` + `json_valid` guard (range / unnest / json_each) | Malformed JSON error | 2 |
| empty filter on view with lateral UNNEST, 3M rows | 0.012 s | 0.008–0.011 s |

Tests: the new test passes. `test/sql/subquery/*`, `test/optimizer/*`, `test/sql/cte/*`, `test/sql/optimizer/*`, `test/sql/json/*` and `test/sql/table_function/*` all pass (tpch/tpcds tests were skipped because those extensions weren't in this build). The code isn't clang-formatted, because there is no clang-format on the build box.

comments.body:
CI fix pushed (94377976318): merged main, and updated two `test/optimizer/deliminator.test` checks that came in with #28649. Dropping the identity projections changes how these plans render:

- The selected-domain `SEMI` now renders above the `MARK` join, so `MARK.*SEMI` no longer matched. The MARK and the domain SEMI are now checked separately.
- Q22's `NOT EXISTS` now plans as an equality `ANTI` join on `c_custkey` instead of `MARK` + `FILTER` (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`). The Q22 check still requires the delim domain `SEMI` on `o_custkey = c_custkey`, and it now also requires the ANTI join on `c_custkey`.

About the **TPCH plan-cost regression on q22** (build 19000 → 38000, probe 190069 → 380138): it comes from the metric, not from a worse plan. `scripts/plan_cost_runner.py` (`is_measured_join`) doesn't count `MARK` joins. On main, the NOT EXISTS stays a MARK join and isn't counted. With this PR it becomes a `RIGHT_ANTI` hash join, which is counted for the first time, and the added cost is exactly that join's inputs. q22 at SF1 takes the same time either way: about 23 ms on both, over 5 runs each.

The Regression Tests failure is the TPC-H q22 plan-cost check (build cost 19000 → 38000, total 190069 → 196453). It is the same result as on the 2026-11-16 run of this PR. q22's correlated `NOT EXISTS` now plans an ANTI join where main has a MARK join, and `scripts/plan_cost_runner.py` does not count MARK joins (`is_measured_join`). So main's cost leaves that join out, while this branch counts it. The plan-cost check therefore compares against a baseline that skips the join. IMDB plan cost shows no differences. The rest of the run is green apart from the Summary job, which only reflects this failure. It needs a maintainer to accept the q22 plan-cost difference.

review_comments.body:
Non-blocking: this check cannot fail with the current data. Every row of `docs` has five items, so the LEFT join has no unmatched rows. As a result, `count(*) = 0` holds whether or not the filter sees null-extended rows.

Could we add a table with an empty list, a missing key and a duplicate id, so the test counts null-extended rows and their duplicates? This example passes on both this PR and main, so it guards the behavior rather than reproducing a bug.

```
statement ok
CREATE TABLE sparse_docs AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    (1, '[{"items": [{"type": "a"}]}]'),
    (2, '[{"items": []}]'),
    (3, '[{"other": 1}]'),
    (3, '[{"other": 1}]')) v(id, doc);

query II
SELECT id, count(*)
FROM sparse_docs LEFT JOIN LATERAL unnest(CAST(json_extract(sparse_docs.doc, '$[0].items') AS JSON[])) AS i(item) ON true
WHERE item IS NULL
GROUP BY id ORDER BY id;
----
2	1
3	2
```

@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+# name: test/sql/subquery/lateral/lateral_filter_into_delim_cte.test
+# description: Filters reach the lateral UNNEST or table function of a delim join that was rewritten into CTEs
+# group: [lateral]
+
+require json
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE notes AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
+    (1, '[{"kind": "X", "n": 1}]'),
+    (2, '[{"kind": "Y"}]'),
+    (3, 'a free text note, not JSON')) v(id, payload);
+
+# a guard on the input of a lateral table function also protects it inside a correlated subquery
+query I
+SELECT count(*) FROM notes d
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM notes AS a, range(0, CAST(coalesce(json_array_length(a.payload), 0) AS BIGINT)) AS t(i)
+    WHERE a.id = d.id AND json_valid(a.payload)
+      AND json_extract_string(json_extract(a.payload, '$[' || t.i || ']'), '$.kind') = 'X');
+----
+2
+
+query I
+SELECT d.id FROM notes d
+WHERE EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM notes AS a, range(0, CAST(coalesce(json_array_length(a.payload), 0) AS BIGINT)) AS t(i)
+    WHERE a.id = d.id AND json_valid(a.payload)
+      AND json_extract_string(json_extract(a.payload, '$[' || t.i || ']'), '$.kind') = 'X')
+ORDER BY d.id;
+----
+1
+
+query I
+SELECT count(*) FROM notes d
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM notes AS a, unnest(CAST(a.payload AS JSON[])) AS t(item)
+    WHERE a.id = d.id AND json_valid(a.payload) AND json_extract_string(t.item, '$.kind') = 'X');
+----
+2
+
+query I
+SELECT count(*) FROM notes d
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM notes AS a, LATERAL (SELECT unnest(CAST(a.payload AS JSON[])) AS item) t
+    WHERE a.id = d.id AND json_valid(a.payload) AND json_extract_string(t.item, '$.kind') = 'X');
+----
+2
+
+query I
+SELECT count(*) FROM notes d
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM notes AS a, json_each(a.payload) AS t
+    WHERE a.id = d.id AND json_valid(a.payload) AND json_extract_string(t.value, '$.kind') = 'X');
+----
+2
+
+statement ok
+CREATE TABLE docs AS
+SELECT i AS id,
+       to_json([{'id': i, 'items': [{'id': j, 'type': CASE WHEN j = 0 THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END} FOR j IN range(5)]}]) AS doc
+FROM range(4) t(i);
+
+# a filter that can throw on the unnested side of an inner lateral join is applied to the unnest output
+query II
+EXPLAIN (FORMAT compact) SELECT count(*)
+FROM docs, unnest(CAST(docs.doc AS JSON[])) AS t(thread), unnest(CAST(json_extract(thread, '$.items') AS JSON[])) AS i(item)
+WHERE json_extract_string(item, '$.type') = 'a';
+----
+physical_plan	<REGEX>:.*FILTER[^\n]*json_extract_string\(item, '\$\.type'\) = 'a'[^\n]*\n( *PROJECTION[^\n]*\n)* *INOUT_FUNCTION[^\n]*Name: unnest.*
+
+query I
+SELECT count(*)
+FROM docs, unnest(CAST(docs.doc AS JSON[])) AS t(thread), unnest(CAST(json_extract(thread, '$.items') AS JSON[])) AS i(item)
+WHERE json_extract_string(item, '$.type') = 'a';
+----
+4
+
+# above a LEFT lateral join, the filter has to see the rows without a match

review_comments.body: Good point, thanks. Added in 73a11676acb: `sparse_docs`, with an empty list, a missing key and a duplicate outer row, so the null-extended rows and their duplicates are actually counted (`2 → 1`, `3 → 2`). I kept the original query next to it.
